newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp debt issuers get set to pitch some deals.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp debt issuers get set to pitch some deals.

text.p: A busy week is expected for the corporate bond primary market as several issuers get set to pitch their offerings and anxious investors run to snatch up the debt, dealers said.
"There's talk of several deals in the market...there continues to be a lot of investor demand for corporate paper," one syndicate source said.
Nationwide Financial is expected to step up to the new issue plate with a $400 million two-part debt offering, syndicate sources said.
The first part is expected to consist of $300 million A1/A-plus rated 30-year debt, callable after 10 years, sources said.
The second tranche is expected to consist of $100 million in A1/A rated 40-year capital securities, sources added.
Nationwide's deal is expected to be launched today and priced on Tuesday, they added.
Meanwhile, McKesson Corp is said to be in the bull pen warming up to bring their $525 million three-part debt offering via Chase Securities, syndicate sources said.
The first tranche is expected to consist of $175 million three-year notes, the second part, $175 million in five-year debt, and the final tranche, $175 million in 30-year debt, sources said.
McKesson's offering is expected to be rated A3/A, sources added.
Another $800 million is expected to come to market out of Tennessee Gas Pipeline, which is said to be lining up a three-part debt offering for this week, market sources said.
The deal is expected to consist of a 20-year issue, a 30-year with a 10-year put option, and a 40-year, they added.
